title: Fail CI when the complete target query-port method inventory is stale or ambiguous

requirements.invariant: The inventory records target query-port declarations as technical evidence only. It cannot promote current source behavior, a protocol spelling, or generated output into product authority.

This shared technical-control slice inventories query-port requirements without claiming a product slice, logical access design, physical index, or adapter implementation. Every generated method becomes an explicit downstream input to the logical access/index crosswalk.
Every claimed control surface, requirement, generated artifact, test owner, exclusion, downstream obligation and status transition is named before executable implementation begins.

The exact parser and negative-test contract is frozen at READY, executable implementation follows a green immutable READY checkpoint, and generated output is reviewed before any downstream query or index mapping advances.

READY, implementation and promotion checkpoints use exact allowlists, record deterministic commands and artifacts, preserve production isolation, and never describe machine freshness as human semantic review.

Every direct method requirement in a public LedgerTargetCore protocol ending exactly Querying is inventoried as a read-port method without deriving command, repository, persistence or product semantics from it.

The inventory generator and tests are dependency-free Node controls over repository Swift text and conversion metadata; they import no Firebase, Supabase, PowerSync, SQL-driver or Swift-runtime dependency and contact no hosted system.

Stable method identities survive signature evolution while separate signature hashes expose contract drift, allowing later backends and indexes to map reviewed query capabilities without coupling views to a provider.

The scanner includes every direct instance function of every public protocol whose name ends exactly Querying, including non-public requirements, classifies watch-prefixed selectors as observation and reserves request_response for future non-watch methods, and fails closed rather than silently losing unsupported syntax.

The reviewed baseline is exactly 17 implemented-or-later owning surfaces, 17 public Querying protocols and 19 direct methods, all presently watch-prefixed, including exactly two multi-method protocols. Owner resolution is exact through the conversion manifest; only implemented, verified, rehearsed and cutover_ready owners are admitted, while every earlier, blocked, retired or unknown lifecycle rejects.

Ubuntu conversion control runs query-port inventory testing and checking, and the macOS target-environment job explicitly depends on that control job so Swift tests cannot start after a missing, stale, malformed, ambiguous or unparseable inventory result. Checking never rewrites tracked artifacts.

requirements.section: Definition of Done for a Vertical Slice
requirements.invariant: Fresh target query-port inventory is prerequisite evidence only. It does not prove a product slice's predicates, ordering, pagination, readiness, local results, security, Sync, migration, reconciliation or end-to-end behavior.

The target-port inventory follows the existing deterministic generated-inventory discipline while remaining a distinct target contract: stable rows, source digests and checked artifacts make repository changes visible without claiming runtime activity.

Generated TQUERY rows identify backend-neutral target port methods, not Firestore query-builder syntax. A later logical access/index crosswalk must review every generated TQUERY before any physical database or local index design is claimed.

Mechanical completeness is limited to direct instance-method requirements in public LedgerTargetCore protocols ending exactly Querying. A separate downstream reconciliation must account for all 386 QUERY-* source occurrences; neither inventory proves source-query completeness, runtime use or index sufficiency.

items: Each generated row records one stable TQUERY ID derived only from owner surface ID, protocol name and selector, plus a separate normalized signature hash, owner path/status, protocol, selector, category and canonical signature.

The lexical scanner masks comments and strings, tracks nested Swift delimiters, supports multiline/attribute/generic/async/throws/return/where syntax and either emits every direct requirement or rejects the entire inventory.
Output order and JSON/Markdown bytes are deterministic, contain no timestamps and are invariant to CRLF, harmless whitespace and masked comment/string contents.

Today the exact accepted baseline is 17 implemented-or-later owners, 17 public Querying protocols and 19 methods; all 19 are observation methods and the two multi-method protocols are ClientProjectDirectoryQuerying and OperationQuerying.
Owner lifecycle is emitted for review but does not affect TQUERY identity, signature hash or inventory digest; a status-only transition does change generated JSON/Markdown bytes.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This slice inventories application-port declarations and creates no Postgres relation, constraint, view, function, logical access path or physical index.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No query handler, RPC, transaction, lock or command-side behavior is implemented.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema, relation, function or grant is introduced.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No row access is implemented or authorized; owner-manifest validation is repository metadata validation, not user authorization.

syncStreams.notApplicable: No PowerSync Stream, visibility rule, local table or synchronized row is designed or implemented.

localOffline.notApplicable: No query readiness, local result, restart, rejection, queue or durability behavior is added; those remain owned by each query contract.

storageMedia.notApplicable: The inventory contains declarations and hashes only and reads or writes no media reference or bytes.

appMcp.notApplicable: No app or MCP query endpoint is added or changed, and no runtime Swift manifest is introduced.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase source data is read or transformed. Reconciliation of the 386 QUERY-* source occurrences is a named later control slice.

items: Package commands expose generate, check and test modes; check is read-only and reports exact missing/stale/ambiguous inventory failures without rewriting files.

Ubuntu CI runs inventory tests and checking in conversion control; the macOS target-environment job declares that control job as a prerequisite, so target Swift tests and builds do not start after inventory failure. The generated JSON/Markdown diff remains mandatory human-review evidence.
Machine success proves deterministic completeness and freshness only; evidence must explicitly record human review of generated additions, removals and signature changes.

READY may change only the two comment scaffolds, dossier/evidence/control metadata and deliberately re-acknowledged conversion discoverer; it creates no generated inventory artifact or package/workflow hook.

Implementation may replace the two exact leaves, add only target-query-port-inventory.generated.json/.md, the frozen package commands, the Ubuntu conversion-control hook and the target-environment job dependency, while preserving all 16 query owners and existing support surfaces at their prior status.
Promotion is a separate documentation/control checkpoint after immutable implementation CI; reverting this additive control changes no target runtime and no Firebase production behavior.

verification.expected: Repository fixture proves exactly 17 implemented-or-later owner surfaces, 17 exact-suffix public Querying protocols, 19 direct methods, all watch observations, and the exact two multi-method protocol method sets with one row per requirement.
Repeated runs and CRLF, harmless whitespace and masked comment/string variants emit byte-identical sorted JSON/Markdown, stable TQUERY IDs and signature hashes without timestamps.

Added, removed or renamed protocols/methods and independent label, parameter/return type, generic, attribute, async, throws and where-clause changes make checked output stale while method identity and signature hash remain separate.

Multiline declarations, attributes, nested generics and where clauses parse; comments, strings, implementations, extensions, private/internal protocols and non-exact Querying names are excluded without hiding direct requirements.

Unsupported direct functions, malformed/ambiguous declarations, duplicate selectors/overloads, empty Querying protocols, missing/ambiguous manifest owner and every pre-implementation, blocked, retired or unknown owner status reject the full inventory with stable diagnostics.
Missing JSON or Markdown and stale bytes fail; check never writes; generate then check is clean; package generate/check/test commands are exact and dependency-free.

FILE-063B0E6EC659, MAN-INDEX-001, FILE-208B7E9D7F47 and the 16 previously verified query owners preserve lifecycle and ownership; the implemented Space-list owner is added explicitly, while generated TQUERY-to-logical-access and 386 QUERY-* reconciliation remain separate controls.

verification.owner: Ubuntu conversion-control CI and human generated-diff review
verification.expected: Immutable CI runs inventory test/check in the Ubuntu conversion-control job, makes the macOS target-environment job depend on its success, and rejects stale inventory before target Swift tests can start; evidence separately records human review of the generated diff and does not claim logical/physical query design, product behavior or production authority.
